subject.title: Feature: Streaming TTS pipeline for voice calls (sentence-level LLM→TTS→audio)

question: Should streaming telephony become a narrow public speech runtime contract now, or remain private to the voice-call plugin until Twilio and a second transport prove the cancellation and partial-failure semantics?
rationale: Current main supplies the provider audio-stream primitive but has no permanent telephony stream result or agreed recovery policy after partial playback; automation cannot safely choose that public API boundary.

options.title: Public telephony stream
options.body: Add a narrow format/sample-rate-aware streaming contract and prove it end to end with one speech provider and Twilio before adding other transports.

options.title: Private adapter first
options.body: Consume generic speech streams inside voice-call and defer SDK expansion until a second transport implementation validates the abstraction.

options.title: Realtime-only latency path
options.body: Keep classic calls buffered and treat full-duplex realtime providers as the supported low-latency architecture.

recommendation.title: Public telephony stream
recommendation.body: Add a narrow format/sample-rate-aware streaming contract and prove it end to end with one speech provider and Twilio before adding other transports.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans both the voice-call implementation and the public plugin/runtime boundary needed for this decision.
